text:
The Devils came back from 4-2 down to beat the Islanders 5-4 in overtime on Saturday, Jack Hughes finishing it on a breakaway, and it was their fourth straight win. Three straight games to overtime, too. That's the noisy part. The quiet part is better.

New Jersey takes 59 percent of the five-on-five expected goals (the quality of chances), which is elite, and it stays out of the box: 2.53 penalties taken a game, 3.76 drawn. Our race model has them at 24.3 deserved points against 24 actual: no luck either way. The record is the play.

The reason the Devils aren't higher is in net. The goaltending, Connor Hellebuyck's included, has allowed about seven more goals than the chances against them would predict. If that turns, this team runs away with things. Arseny Gritsyuk has 10 points in his last ten on the Jesper Bratt and Hughes line, which has outscored teams 11-3, and Luke Hughes has made the leap The Hockey News keeps writing about: the Brett Pesce and Luke Hughes pair has outscored opponents 18-9. Saturday also brought a fight between Luke Hughes and Matthew Schaefer. We doubt it's the last time those two teams get heated.
headline: New Jersey might be the East's best team on process
